scenes.title:
Fast enough?
Know **before** you run it.
scenes.sub: Big-O ignores seconds. It asks: when the input grows, how fast do the steps grow?

say.say: Will your solution be fast enough? You can know before you run it.

say: Big-O ignores seconds. It asks one question: when the input grows, how fast do the steps grow?

scenes.label: THE STORY
scenes.title: 1,000 answer sheets

items.head: NOT SORTED
items.text: Flip through one by one. On a bad day: **1,000 looks**.

items.head: SORTED BY ROLL NUMBER
items.text: Open the middle, drop the half that can't hold yours. **{{LOOKS}} looks** at most.

say.say: Your teacher has a thousand answer sheets, and you want yours.

say: If they're in no order, you flip through them one by one. On a bad day, you look at all one thousand.

say.say: If they're sorted by roll number, open the middle and drop the half that can't hold yours. Ten looks, at most.
Let's read the cost straight from code. Start a counter at zero.
Loop over every item, and add one each time.
Return the count. It's exactly n.
Ten items, ten steps. A thousand items, a thousand steps. The steps grow with n, so it's O of n.
say.show: Ten items, ten steps. A thousand items, a thousand steps. The steps grow with n, so it's O(n).

say.say: Now, what if we put a loop inside a loop?
For every x, the inner loop runs over all n items again. So we count n times n.
Ten items take a hundred steps. A thousand items take a million. That's O of n squared.
say.show: Ten items take 100 steps. A thousand items take 1,000,000. That's O(n²).

say.say: The third shape halves the input every step, like the sorted answer sheets.
Cut n in half, count one step, and repeat while more than one is left.
A thousand takes nine steps. A million takes only nineteen. That's O of log n.
say.show: 1,000 takes 9 steps. 1,000,000 takes only 19. That's O(log n).

say.say: Here they are side by side. Reading one item, like the first one, is always one step: O of 1.
say.show: Here they are side by side. Reading one item, like nums[0], is always one step: O(1).

say: Log n and n grow slowly, and steadily.

say.say: n squared explodes. A thousand items already take a million steps.

scenes.label: THE TRAP
scenes.title: Loops in a row don't multiply

wrong.head: TWO LOOPS, ONE AFTER THE OTHER

note.text: 2n is still O(n): Big-O drops the constant.

say.say: Here's the trap. Two loops, one after the other, over a thousand items, take two thousand steps. That's still O of n.
say.show: Here's the trap. Two loops, one after the other, over 1,000 items take 2,000 steps. That's still O(n).

say.say: Only a loop inside a loop multiplies, to a million steps.
say.show: Only a loop inside a loop multiplies, to 1,000,000 steps.

say.say: Two n is still O of n. Big-O drops the constant.
say.show: 2n is still O(n). Big-O drops the constant.

items.head: O(1) SPACE
items.text: A few variables, like `steps`. Same size for any input.

items.head: O(n) SPACE
items.text: A new array, set or map that can hold all n items.

say.say: Memory counts the same way. A few variables, like our step counter, is O of 1 space.
say.show: Memory counts the same way. A few variables, like steps, is O(1) space.

say.say: A new array, set, or map that can hold all n items is O of n space. Many fast solutions trade memory for time.
say.show: A new array, set or map that can hold all n items is O(n) space. Many fast solutions trade memory for time.
